claims.text: The baseline material is a predominantly single-phase HEA solid solution without deliberately introduced lubricant precipitates.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 2–5 at.% WS2 followed by aging at approximately 600–800 °C.
The proposed alloying and aging treatment will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale WS2 precipitates within the HEA.
WS2 is a high-temperature-stable solid-lubricant phase.
Dispersed WS2 precipitates will be exposed during sliding.
Exposed WS2 precipitates will form a continuous lubricious tribolayer on the contact surface.
WS2 precipitates will smear over the contact surface during sliding.
The WS2-derived tribolayer will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
The low shear strength of WS2 will promote continuous lubrication.
Continuous lubrication by the WS2-derived tribolayer will reduce friction relative to the untreated HEA.
Continuous lubrication by the WS2-derived tribolayer will reduce wear relative to the untreated HEA.
The modified alloy will exhibit an approximately 20–40% lower steady-state coefficient of friction than the untreated HEA from room temperature to 600 °C.
The modified alloy will exhibit an approximately 30–50% lower wear rate than the untreated HEA from room temperature to 600 °C.
The improvement requires the WS2 precipitates to remain nanoscale and uniformly distributed.
Oxidation of WS2 can degrade the proposed lubrication mechanism.
Operating above the thermal-stability limit of WS2 can degrade the proposed lubrication mechanism.
Excessive precipitate coarsening during processing can negate the lubrication benefit.
